# Cryptographic fixtures

`quais-crypto.json` is generated offline by `../generate-fixtures.mjs` against
the repository's locked `quais@1.0.0-alpha.57` package. It contains **public test
keys only**. Never fund these addresses. Regenerate from the repository root:

```sh
node crates/quai-crypto/tests/generate-fixtures.mjs
```

`bip340.csv` is the official BIP340 vector file downloaded on 2026-09-11 from
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bitcoin/bips/master/bip-0340/test-vectors.csv
Its SHA256 is
`34c9d1d9c3a88d524bc80778540dc43f8306ec249a7485293063c376db851c2d`.
The fixed local bytes are used by tests; tests do not fetch mutable upstream
content. Indexes 0–3 and 15–18 include signing material and explicit auxiliary
values; all 19 cases are used for verification. The auxiliary signing entry
point is crate-private so applications cannot accidentally select deterministic
zero auxiliary randomness through the normal public signing API.

These fixtures establish behavior relative to their references. They do not
establish node transaction acceptance, hardware side-channel resistance or
production wallet safety.

BIP340 is authored by Pieter Wuille, Jonas Nick and Tim Ruffing. Its
[specification metadata](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0340.mediawiki)
licenses code under `BSD-2-Clause OR MIT OR CC0-1.0`; the vector file is retained
under the offered CC0-1.0 option, with this source attribution.

`ordered-musig.json` contains eleven ordered aggregation cases generated by
`../generate-aggregate-fixtures.mjs` using locked
`@brandonblack/musig@0.0.1-alpha.1` and the pinned quais.js crypto adapter.
It includes public toy scalars 1, 2 and 3, full aggregate public keys and JS MuSig
signatures. The generator's deterministic nonce material is only for public
fixtures and must never be used with real keys.

`ordered-musig-rust.json` is a captured copy augmented with signatures from
`cargo run -p quai-crypto --example generate_local_aggregate_signatures`.
That example uses the public local signing API with OS auxiliary randomness,
so regenerated signatures and the file hash change. The independent Go oracle
verifies both JS and Rust signatures against its own ordered aggregate point.
Regenerate the JS baseline with:

```sh
node crates/quai-crypto/tests/generate-aggregate-fixtures.mjs
```

See the Go oracle README for independent verification and the recorded report.
